guard: folding a seeded APPEND LOG into the journal's ordered view, not only into its keyed one
why: The defect this grades was LIVE on the resume path, not hypothetical: the stream is append-only
(one step is a pending record and a settled one), `RunJournalAppender.steps()` replays both, and
the driver seeds a journal straight from that array. `byKey` folded and `order` did not, so the
journal's two views disagreed -- the ceiling counted one step while `entries()` reported two, and
`orphans()` handed the migrate table the same decision twice.
THIS SUITE IS FAIL-FAST: `ok()` THROWS. A mutation must therefore be no broader than the cell it
names, or it kills an earlier cell and grades WRONG-RED, and the completion marker has to be the
FIRST cell rather than the last -- a marker at the end is absent on every genuine kill and would

mutations.name: the seed does not fold: every log row is pushed to the ordered view
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: the ORDERED view folds too — one step is one entry
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: the ORDERED view folds too — one step is one entry
mutations.note: The defect exactly as it shipped. It also reddens the orphan cell below, which is the point: one fold, two consumers.

mutations.name: the fold keeps the FIRST write instead of the last
mutations.replace:
if (!this.byKey.has(full)) this.byKey.set(full, e);
      // FOLD THE LOG.
mutations.expectRed: and it is the LAST write, so a step that settled reads settled
mutations.cell: and it is the LAST write, so a step that settled reads settled
mutations.note: WHICH row survives is a separate claim from WHETHER it folds. First-write-wins folds just as tidily and reports every completed step as still pending -- a resumed run would re-perform work the journal holds a result for. Graded on its own cell because the mutation above cannot distinguish it.

mutations.name: the fold collapses every step to one entry
mutations.expectRed: steps the new program never reached are orphans
mutations.cell: steps the new program never reached are orphans
mutations.note: The narrowness twin, RE-AIMED at the cell that actually fires. A collapsing fold satisfies the first mutation perfectly and erases a run's history, so it must be graded -- but this suite is FAIL-FAST, and the collapse reddens `steps the new program never reached are orphans` (journal.smoke:152) long before the fold's own block is reached. Naming a later cell graded WRONG-RED: the suite exited 1 for a true reason at an assertion that was not the one under test, which is indistinguishable from a kill only if nobody reads which cell died. The block's own narrowness cell is kept -- a reader of the fold looks there, not 400 lines up -- and is redundant for THIS mutation, which is recorded rather than hidden.

mutations.name: the fold reorders history by completion
mutations.expectRed: and they keep the order the run PERFORMED them in, not the order they finished in
mutations.cell: and they keep the order the run PERFORMED them in, not the order they finished in
mutations.note: The second narrowness twin, and the one a reader would call equivalent: last-occurrence ordering folds correctly and keeps every step, and silently reports a concurrent run doing its work in an order it never did. `order` is the order steps BEGAN, because that is when a step's pending row is written.
